newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government slams industrialist's criticism.
newsitem.headline: Italian government slams industrialist's criticism.

text.p: The Italian government on Sunday slammed Giorgio Fossa, head of the influential Confindustria industrialists group, for making scathing remarks against the centre-left administration.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said Fossa had "expressed his views in a direct way -- perhaps a bit to directly".
"Certainly, to make his point he exaggerated a bit," former prime minister Dini was quoted as telling La Repubblica daily.

Fossa had said Prime Minister Romano Prodi government's days were numbered if it did not do more to help business. "If the government doesn't change course, the country itself will sweep it away," he told a business convention in Milan.

Gerardo Bianco, leader of the centrist Popular Party which is part of the governing coalition, said he was surprised by Fossa, "who just four days ago expressed his appreciation for the government's economic policy".
"Anyway, I'm sure he'll 'correct' what he said in a few days' time -- the opinions of the industrialists change all too often," Bianco said.
In his speech, Fossa said the government should make it easier for private business to create jobs but instead "it raises taxes and therefore does not understand the reality of the country."
Bianco said: "I just wish the industrialists would make some solid proposals because nobody knows what they want."

Mauro Zani of the ex-communist Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the largest coalition party, also criticised Fossa, whose comments were welcomed by members of the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance.
"Such a radical statement by a man who holds such an important position in our economy is on the limits of irresponsibility," Zani told reporters on Saturday.
